title: Sir Anthony Mildmay, Knight of Apethorpe, Northamptonshire
medium: Watercolor on vellum, laid on card, mounted on wood

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund

source.label: Wikipedia: “He mostly painted small oval miniatures, but also some larger cabinet miniatures, up to about 10 inches (25 centimetres) tall”
Wikipedia: Hilliard was “best known for his portrait miniatures”
Cleveland Museum of Art record: a portrait of Sir Anthony Mildmay

work.text: Despite its small scale, this portrait reveals Nicholas Hilliard’s emulation of (and rivalry with) life-size court portraiture, while his meticulous attention to detail and use of costly materials like shell gold reflect the refined world of courtly tournaments.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art

moment.text: This train of thought leads him on to recall a conversation that he once had with Sir Philip Sidney, who asked him how he could express on a small scale the difference in figure between a tall man and a short one.

source.author: Philip Norman
source.title: Introductory note on Nicholas Hilliard’s Treatise concerning ‘The Arte of Limning’
source.publisher: The Walpole Society, vol. 1 (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: Framed by the folds of a circular tent, Sir Anthony Mildmay strikes a relaxed and confident pose, with his right hand resting on a cloth-covered table and his left grasping the hilt of his thin, double-edged sword called a rapier. Helmet, gauntlet, and leg coverings are scattered about, as if Mildmay has been interrupted in the act of putting on or taking off his armor.
